profilePeriod: Reform UK leadership, 2024–30 September 2026; dated earlier personal and ideological context.

sources.title: Reform UK current policies
sources.evidence: Tax-funded NHS; stricter visas and English fluency; expanded stop-and-search and prisons; lower taxes; nuclear energy; defence spending commitment. Party proposals, not proven policy effects.

sources.title: Farage: first 100 days conference speech
sources.evidence: Proposes parliamentary emergency sittings, adding peers or a Lords referendum, limiting judicial obstacles and removing obstructive officials; seeks an electoral majority.

sources.title: Reform UK Scotland manifesto
sources.evidence: Pages 9–10 support councils raising and retaining revenues; page 17 criticises police centralisation; NHS remains tax-funded; local public housing and public-private infrastructure coexist with rent deregulation.

sources.title: Farage on first ministers meeting
sources.evidence: PA report quotes Farage treating Scottish independence as settled for a generation following its referendum.

sources.title: Farage on anti-disinformation unit
sources.evidence: Acknowledges foreign bots but opposes state policing of lawful political speech.

sources.title: ITV direct interview on cannabis and defence
sources.evidence: Withdraws earlier enthusiasm for cannabis decriminalisation inquiry; supports stronger forces facing Russia-China-North Korea; favours publicly funded STEM tuition.

sources.title: Farage authored column against capital punishment
sources.evidence: Personally opposes the death penalty while defending public debate; earlier context rather than a new pledge.

sources.title: Farage on IRGC
sources.evidence: Demands IRGC terrorist proscription and stronger response to Iranian threats against British security.

sources.title: LBC interview: Britain should not join Iran war
sources.evidence: Headline and interview establish reluctance to join American war in Iran; distinguishes allied solidarity from automatic participation. Exact publication date not recovered.

sources.title: Reform small-business plan
sources.evidence: Supports SMEs through lighter regulation, tax relief and easier financing.

sources.title: Farage interview on US tariffs
sources.evidence: Direct remarks advocate UK-US free trade deal and criticise failure to escape American import duties; trade openness does not imply EU political membership.

sources.title: Reform crypto bill executive summary
sources.evidence: Search-indexed primary executive summary promotes UK cryptocurrency and blockchain innovation. Direct PDF open failed; relied only on visible indexed text.

sources.title: High Profile direct interview
sources.evidence: Christian values treated as cultural and moral resources; recalls adult nonbelief and uncertainty following a plane crash; not a claim of present devout faith.

sources.title: Reform proposal to protect Christian heritage
sources.evidence: Reports Reform spokesman Yusuf proposing protected church status and preserving Christian national heritage. Party context, not evidence of Farage personal theology.

sources.title: Farage abortion remarks
sources.evidence: Calls himself pro-choice but objects to 24-week limit; indexed reporting recovered despite direct open failure.

sources.title: Farage LBC remarks on same-sex marriage
sources.evidence: Opposed introduction and preferred civil partnerships; now treats legal same-sex marriage as settled rather than proposing repeal.

sources.title: ITV Border direct interview on AI data centres
sources.evidence: Supports pause on hyperscale centres after reconsidering effects on people and farms, differing from Reform MSPs.

sources.title: The Purple Revolution publisher listing
sources.evidence: Nigel Farage author; subtitle The Year That Changed Everything; book on UKIP strategy, EU and sovereignty; first publication 2015.

sources.title: Portuguese-market listing of original-language book
sources.evidence: Searches for Brazilian or Portuguese translation found only original title and unrelated works; no verified Brazilian translation.

facts: Party promotes local fiscal autonomy in Scotland (April 2026).
estrutura.tension: Local service autonomy within a sovereign union; Brexit is not evidence for unlimited regional secession.

facts: Seeks elections and plebiscites but would weaken judicial and Lords resistance to a mandate (September 2026).
representacao.tension: Majoritarian representative democracy, not permanent unelected dictatorship or leaderless assemblies.

facts: Tough policing coexists with opposition to speech censorship.
Cannabis caution (2024) and personal opposition to execution (2014).
poder.tension: Civil liberties are selective; do not equate security policy with universal state surveillance.

facts: September platform requires English fluency and restricts immigration.
imigracao.tension: Assimilation and national borders, not abolition of all personal cultural customs.

facts: Strong armed forces and deterrence (2024–2026); IRGC proscription urged September 2026.
diplomacia.tension: Defence strength is compatible with reluctance about particular wars.

facts: British sovereignty and threats from Iran central to current rhetoric; opposes automatic UK participation in Iran war.
intervencao.tension: Assertive national interests and close US links coexist with war restraint.

facts: September platform retains NHS taxation; August business plan favours private enterprise.
economia.tension: Mixed provision and social housing prevent treating him as an anarchocapitalist.

facts: Tax cuts and deregulation prominent; Scotland programme also uses public-private infrastructure and local housing.
controle.tension: Market-led economy with targeted national-sector intervention, not total laissez-faire or full planning.

facts: March 2025 remarks explicitly seek US free trade.
comercio.tension: National energy security and British-worker preference temper openness; exiting EU political authority does not mean autarky.

facts: Personal faith uncertainty in 2011; Christian heritage policy in 2026.
religiao.tension: Cultural Christianity rather than divine law overruling elected statute; personal contemporary belief uncertain.

facts: 2025 remarks accept early abortion choice but seek shorter limit; gay marriage treated as settled despite previous opposition.
moral.tension: Traditionalism does not entail criminalising all private adult conduct.

facts: Pro-nuclear and crypto policies; September 2026 AI-centre pause after local-impact concerns.
tecnologia.tension: Industrial modernisation with constraints; no sourced transhumanist or embryo-enhancement platform.

limitations: Simulation, not actual survey responses. Brazilian examples are translated functionally into British institutions and interests.

Weak direct evidence on facial recognition, weapons ownership, central-bank design, embryo editing and brain implants. Modest answers are contextual inferences, not attributed quotations; N reserved for genuine competing commitments.
Older individual statements are dated and subordinate to current positions. Regional party programme is contextual evidence and not automatically a personal endorsement of every detail.
Research refreshed through 2026-10-01; retained explicit endpoint 30 September 2026. No relevant 1 October change identified. Failed PDF/article opens are distinguished from indexed evidence.

recommendedMetadata.reason: Current PT/EN descriptions accurately include sovereignty, restrictive immigration, taxes, tax-funded NHS, defence and judicial mandate tension; sent coordinator before answering.

bookDecision.reason: Self-authored political account of UKIP strategy and sovereignty. More directly political than Fighting Bull/Flying Free. Publisher confirms authorship and 2015 first edition; no verified Brazilian translation, so retain original. No existing entry to alter.

title.pt: The Purple Revolution: The Year That Changed Everything
title.en: The Purple Revolution: The Year That Changed Everything

processNotes: Read all four controlling documents and saved prompt. Independent research preceded answers; only prior research period and URLs were read, never scores or answers.

Conceptual neighbours: Trump (less blanket tariff emphasis); Thatcher (current NHS and border agenda); Le Pen (stronger free-trade/enterprise roots); Wilders (Christian cultural protection). No numerical targets.
Only own prompt, staged answers and research record written; no shared metadata, books, archives or STATE changes.
All 240 answers independently chosen once, question by question in template order; five archetypes chosen by wording. No score/compatibility target used. No score-based revisions.
Post-generation integrity check confirms the exact questions-template text and freshly generated archetype block; hashes match. Blocker retained for coordinator/user decision, not bypassed.
